subject: Cardstack discovery follow-up: schedule demo + capacity sizing
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cardstack.co>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cardstack discovery follow-up: schedule demo + capacity sizing

Hi David + Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to walk through how Redwood might fit into our inference stack. Quick recap and asks from Cardstack: we run a mix of embedding generation and chat-style completions for search/rerank workflows. High-level numbers:~
- Steady baseline: ~40 QPS (embeddings + short completions)
- Peak window: ~120 QPS sustained for 1.5-2 hours/day (batchy traffic)
- Latency targets: p95 < 120ms for embeddings, p99 < 300ms for completions
- Typical sequence lengths: embeddings 256 tokens, chat 512 tokens

We'd like to lock a technical deep-dive + dedicated capacity sizing call to nail down throughput/latency tradeoffs and the right pool size. Availability next week is slim for our infra lead (Miguel), but he can join Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Proposed outcome for the next call:
- Confirm model families and quantization tolerance (we can share test prompts)
- Agree on required GPU pool sizing and baseline autoscaling policy
- Define a short mutual action plan (deliverables + owners)

Attached: a short ops load-profile spreadsheet and our initial SLO sketch (attachment stubs).

Could you propose 2 windows that work for your engineering folks? Also please send any sizing intake form you prefer we fill ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Elena
VP Engineering
Cardstack

Attachment: Cardstack_OPS_Load_Profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cardstack.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cardstack discovery follow-up: schedule demo + capacity sizing

Elena — really appreciate the concise load numbers, that helps a lot. Monica and I reviewed and I looped in Grace (performance engineer) to lead the sizing discussion.

We can run a 45-60 minute technical deep-dive focused on: topology (model variant + quantization), batching strategy, KV cache behavior for chat, and autoscaling thresholds. If that looks good we can follow immediately with a 30-45 minute dedicated capacity sizing session (pool sizing + SLO alignment).

Two slots that work for our engineering team:
- Tue, 12 May 2027 · 10:00–11:00 PT (deep-dive + sizing back-to-back)
- Wed, 13 May 2027 · 14:00–15:00 PT (alternate)

We also have a standardized intake form that helps us estimate pool footprint. Please see attached Redwood_Sizing_Intake_Form.pdf — filling the fields for peak sequence distribution, concurrency, and token mix reduces back-and-forth.

If Miguel needs to join, happy to include him — feel free to CC his email when you confirm. I'll draft a short mutual action plan after we lock the slot.

Best,
David Kim
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Sizing_Intake_Form.pdf (1 page intake)

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700

Thanks — Tue 12 May 10:00 PT works for us. I CC'd Miguel (infra) and copied our procurement lead in the thread (we'll add them if they require any paperwork). A couple of quick asks before the call:
- Can you confirm which cloud regions have the lowest variance for p99 (we prefer us-west-2 but can be flexible)?
- Are SOC 2 artifacts / security questionnaire answers something we can get ahead of time?

We'll try to complete the intake form this afternoon and upload the sample prompts you mentioned.

See you Tue — please send a calendar invite and any pre-read we should skim.

Cheers,
Elena
VP Engineering, Cardstack
